title: Thailand vs Cambodia: Which Should You Visit?
description: A data-backed comparison of Thailand and Cambodia based on Reddit discussions, real costs, weather data, and traveler preferences.

verdict: Thailand is better if you want First-timers, beach lovers, foodies, party seekers. Cambodia is better if you want History buffs, budget travelers, off-the-beaten-path adventurers. Mid-range budget: Thailand $30–50/day vs Cambodia $20–40/day.

faqs.question: Is Thailand or Cambodia better for first-time visitors to Southeast Asia?
faqs.answer: Thailand is the easier first trip. Tourism infrastructure is more developed — English signage is everywhere, the BTS/MRT in Bangkok is world-class, and accommodation ranges from $5 hostels to $500 resorts. Cambodia is more raw and adventurous, which seasoned travelers love, but it requires more flexibility and tolerance for imperfect roads, power outages, and less English. Reddit consensus: start with Thailand, then add Cambodia on a return trip or as a 4–5 day side trip.

faqs.question: How far apart are Thailand and Cambodia?
faqs.answer: Bangkok to Siem Reap is about 400 km — a 1-hour flight ($60–100) or 8–10 hour bus via the Poipet border ($10–25). Bangkok to Phnom Penh is about 660 km — a 1h15m flight ($70–120). The border crossing is straightforward but can take 1–2 hours for visa processing. Most travelers fly between the two countries.

faqs.question: Is it worth visiting both on the same trip?
faqs.answer: Absolutely, if you have 2+ weeks. A popular combo: 7–10 days Thailand (Bangkok + Chiang Mai or islands) plus 4–5 days Cambodia (Siem Reap for Angkor Wat + maybe Phnom Penh). The cheap, short flight between Bangkok and Siem Reap makes it a no-brainer. If you only have 10 days, most travelers recommend picking one country and exploring it properly rather than rushing both.

faqs.question: Which is cheaper, Thailand or Cambodia?
faqs.answer: Cambodia is slightly cheaper on paper — $0.50 beers, $1 meals, $8 guestrooms. A mid-range day runs $20–40 vs Thailand's $30–50. But Thailand often offers better value: for a few dollars more, quality jumps significantly. The biggest Cambodia expense is Angkor Wat ($37/day pass + $15–25 transport). Budget backpackers stretch further in Cambodia; mid-range travelers often prefer Thailand's price-to-quality ratio.

faqs.question: Is Cambodia safe for tourists?
faqs.answer: Yes, generally safe. Siem Reap is very tourist-friendly with minimal crime. Phnom Penh requires more awareness — phone snatching from motorbikes is the main risk, so keep valuables in a front bag and avoid displaying expensive phones. Avoid Sihanoukville's downtown casino area; go straight to Koh Rong instead. Scams are less common than in heavily touristy parts of Thailand, but always confirm prices upfront for tuk-tuks and tours.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Thailand and Cambodia?
faqs.answer: November through February — the cool, dry season with comfortable 25–33°C temperatures and virtually no rain. Peak tourist season, so prices are higher and popular spots get crowded. March–May is scorching hot (36°C+). The rainy season (May–October in Thailand, June–November in Cambodia) means lower prices and fewer tourists, but expect afternoon downpours and some flooding. April's Songkran festival in Thailand is worth braving the heat for.

faqs.question: Should you choose Thailand or Cambodia for do i need a visa for thailand and cambodia?
faqs.answer: Thailand offers 60-day visa-exempt entry for most Western nationalities — completely free, no application needed. Cambodia requires a tourist visa: $30 on arrival at airports and land borders (bring a passport photo and cash), or apply for an e-visa online before your trip. Cambodia's visa is valid for 30 days, extendable once for another 30 days at a local travel agent for a small fee.

sectionVerdicts.why: Thailand wins on food — not even close. The depth, variety, and quality of Thai cuisine at every price point is extraordinary. But don't sleep on Cambodia's Khmer food; fish amok and lok lak are genuinely world-class dishes.
sectionVerdicts.whoThisMattersFor: Matters most if food quality, variety, or meal budgets will shape your trip between First-timers, beach lovers, foodies, party seekers. and History buffs, budget travelers, off-the-beaten-path adventurers..

sectionVerdicts.why: Cambodia wins for "bucket list" historical impact — Angkor Wat is a once-in-a-lifetime sight and the Killing Fields are important to witness. Thailand offers more breadth (40,000+ temples, royal palaces, living traditions like Songkran) but Cambodia's concentrated intensity is unmatched.
sectionVerdicts.whoThisMattersFor: Matters most if you are choosing based on atmosphere, heritage, and what kind of experience feels more memorable.

sectionVerdicts.why: Cambodia is 15–25% cheaper day-to-day, especially for accommodation and drinks. But Thailand's value-for-money is often better — you get more quality per dollar. Budget backpackers will stretch further in Cambodia; mid-range travelers may prefer Thailand's infrastructure.
sectionVerdicts.whoThisMattersFor: Matters most if nightly rates, meal prices, or transport costs will change how long you can stay.

sectionVerdicts.why: Thailand wins decisively on transport. Getting around is easy, cheap, and comfortable. Cambodia requires more patience and planning, but that's part of the adventure. Budget extra time for overland travel in Cambodia.
sectionVerdicts.whoThisMattersFor: Matters most if you care about ease, transfer friction, and how much time you lose moving between sights.

sectionVerdicts.why: November–February is peak season for a reason — comfortable weather, no rain, perfect conditions. If you're budget-conscious and flexible, the rainy season (June–October) offers great deals and a different, equally beautiful experience.
sectionVerdicts.whoThisMattersFor: Matters most if seasonality, rain, heat, or crowd levels could make or break the trip.

sectionVerdicts.why: Thailand has vastly more accommodation options at every price point, with better quality at mid-range budgets. Cambodia wins on ultra-budget stays — your dollar goes further in Siem Reap and Kampot than almost anywhere in Thailand outside Chiang Mai.
sectionVerdicts.whoThisMattersFor: Matters most if neighborhood choice, hotel value, or day-trip convenience is a big part of the decision.

sectionVerdicts.why: Thailand wins overwhelmingly on beaches. If beach time is your main goal, Thailand is the obvious choice. Cambodia's Koh Rong offers something Thailand's popular islands can't — genuine seclusion and untouched beauty — but the options are limited.
sectionVerdicts.whoThisMattersFor: Matters most if this category is one of your top trip-deciding factors.

sectionVerdicts.why: Thailand has more day trip variety, especially from Bangkok and Chiang Mai. Cambodia's day trips are rewarding but fewer in number. Tonle Sap's floating villages and Kulen Mountain are worth the effort.
sectionVerdicts.whoThisMattersFor: Matters most if you want one base with strong side trips rather than a single-destination stay.

sectionVerdicts.why: If you have 2+ weeks, absolutely do both. The 1-hour flight between Bangkok and Siem Reap makes it a no-brainer. Thailand for the food, beaches, and infrastructure; Cambodia for Angkor Wat, history, and raw authenticity. They pair perfectly.
sectionVerdicts.whoThisMattersFor: Matters most if you are deciding whether this should be a one-destination trip or a broader itinerary.
